Here is a concise description of the video segment:

The video starts with a close-up of a text message. The highlighted text reads, “Well, we are writing to you to see if you might be interested in committing to racing each other at a race other than UTMB this year (2024).” This implies the sender wants the recipient to race in a different competition than UTMB. The scene transitions to a middle-aged man with short gray hair, wearing a dark gray sweater and a microphone, speaking to the camera. Behind him is a white cabinet with red accessories and bottles. The scene transitions to a block of text that reads “First off, we want to acknowledge that UTMB is a great race, even though there has been a lot of drama recently, we still feel that the race and the organization have done a lot of good for the sport of ultra running. Thanks to UTMB, we now have a world championship-esque event that draws many of the best runners in the sport as well as sponsors, media, and fans from all over the world. It has truly become the big event of the year and has really helped to put our sport on the map. Having an event like this has created a lot of opportunity for people like ourselves, as it drives a lot of money and attention to the sport. This, we feel, is a good thing.” The highlighted section of text reads “It has truly become the big event of the year and has really helped to put our sport on the map." This implies that the speaker acknowledges the significant role UTMB has played in growing the sport.

The video segment begins with a text overlay against a light beige background. The text is black and reads: "However, while it may be good for the sport to grow and develop in these ways, it is also important that the growth occurs in a positive, healthy manner. Unfortunately, the current direction that UTMB, UTMB Group, and Ironman have taken has given us cause for concern. There are a multitude of things that we could point to that are concerning to us, but the gist of it is that we feel that they are not managing themselves and their event(s) in a way that has the best interests of the sport and its people in mind.” (English Translation: The provided text expresses concern over the management direction taken by UTMB, UTMB Group, and Ironman, stating that the organization feels their actions don't prioritize the best interests of the sport and its participants.) The text “we feel that they are not managing themselves and their event(s) in a way that has the best interest of the sport and its people in mind” is highlighted in light blue. The text on the screen then changes. The new text reads: “we are alright with the organization making money. However, we feel that there is a way to do this without treating people poorly and running over everyone who gets in your way. To put it simply, we want them to run their business well. We want them to be considerate. We want them to not only ask "what can we do to benefit ourselves?", but also "what can we do to improve the sport of trail running as a whole?". (English Translation: The provided text expresses the sentiment that the organization doesn't mind the UTMB group making money, but would want them to be more considerate about their business practice. It also wants them to ask how they can improve trail running as a whole.) “We want them to not only ask "what can we do to benefit ourselves?", but also "what can we do to improve the sport of trail running as a whole?".” is highlighted in light blue. Following this text, the video transitions to a man, presumably the speaker, sitting on a cream-colored couch in what appears to be a home setting. The man has graying hair, light skin, and is wearing a dark gray sweater with buttons. Behind him, on the wall, hangs a collection of medals and a shelf with various items. Throughout the video segment, the man looks directly at the camera and speaks, gesturing occasionally with his hands.

The video segment opens with a frame showing a text document. The text reads, "Perhaps the best way to communicate our discontent and apply some pressure is to band together and all go to a different race. An absence of the top fifteen ranked male and female runners from the UTMB start line would speak volumes. It would communicate to them that we are not happy and pressure them to make some changes. So, we would like to hear your thoughts. We have already pin-pointed a potential race that we could attend instead of UTMB, but before we get into all that, please let us know what you think. Do you have the same or similar concerns? Are you interested in." The scene then shifts to a middle-aged man with grey hair, wearing a black sweater, sitting on a beige sofa in a room with numerous running medals on the walls. He's speaking directly to the camera, with an earnest expression, sharing details from the previously displayed text. Subsequently, a graphic shows the "WORLD TRAIL MAJORS 2024 SCHEDULE," displaying race names, locations, distances, and elevation gains. The races "Quebec-Canada" and "Cape Town-South Africa" are highlighted with a red line. Then, the middle-aged man reappears to continue speaking, followed by the text "Please let us know so that we can continue the dialogue and discuss what the next steps might be. And please realize, this is not meant to be a malicious, hateful thing towards UTMB. The idea here is to find a way to apply some pressure to the UTMB/Ironman organization so that we can effect positive change. It would be great if one day we could go to UTMB and feel good about it, knowing that what they are doing is making the sport better, not worse." The video concludes with the logo of "Film My Run."
